mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior 8 weeks reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 4% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS change (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by declining unemployment (UNRATE) creates a labor market momentum that is predictive of positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: In a weak labor market regime (UNRATE > 6%), the correlation between PAYEMS and 20-day SPX returns is negative or non-significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer demand proxies (HOUST) coinciding with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a shift from supply-side to demand-side driven market dynamics, predicting positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 10% in a month while INDPRO falls by > 5% in the same month
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, the signal is not statistically predictive of SPX returns (p > 0.05 in rolling window OLS).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 50-week moving average, when sustained for at least 3 months, indicates persistent supply-side weakness that is associated with negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: During supply contraction phases, the 20-day forward return is not significantly different from the mean of the prior 12 months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate crosses above 2% for the first time in a tightening cycle, it triggers a risk premium adjustment that is associated with negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2% for the first time in a rising FEDFUNDS regime
regime_hint: inflation accelerating in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: Inflation crosses back below 2% without a subsequent SPX loss (p > 0.05 in regime-split OLS).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% coinciding with a sharp rise in labor force participation (PAYEMS) creates optimism about economic strength, predicting positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% in a single month while PAYEMS increases by > 1% in the same month
failure_condition: The effect is not significant in a contractionary labor market regime (UNRATE > 5%) (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2 consecutive month decline in consumer confidence proxies (not available in the given catalog) cannot be used; instead, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below trend while retail sales (not available) cannot be used either. Instead, a sustained drop in GDP deflator (not available) is unavailable. Thus, we use: A 3-month decline in the S&P 500 itself as a negative demand signal, predicting negative 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns do not show a statistically significant negative relationship with INDPRO declines (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate remains unchanged for 4 consecutive months in a regime of persistent market volatility (indirectly inferred from high GDPC1 volatility), it predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as investors anticipate a potential rate cut.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS on hold for 4 months with GDPC1 volatility > 15% in the preceding month
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 days when the trigger is not met or volatility remains low (p > 0.05).
